title: Coverage by instrument
intro: Which instrument images the emulator has been run against, and how: a row per image, a column per way of running it or test. The in-emulation columns run the instrument's image in emulation from power-on, without its 1 PPS input under test; the hardware columns run the instrument itself; the leap second columns run oncore-host's test hooks against the image. A Yes, Partial or In review links to where the repository records it, and the generator checks that the section is there.

columns.title: oncore-host
columns.means: oncore-host on a PC, a u-blox through gpsd, against the instrument's image in emulation.

columns.title: Board
columns.means: The emulator board on the jig, against the image in emulation.

columns.title: oncore-host, instrument
columns.means: oncore-host on a PC feeding the instrument's own GPS port.

columns.title: Board in instrument
columns.means: The emulator board in the instrument in place of its VP Oncore.

columns.title: Leap second pending
columns.means: oncore-host --leap-pending against the image in emulation: the image reports the scheduled leap second (:PTIM:LEAP:ACC?, :STAT?, :DATE?, :DUR? and its status screen).

columns.title: Leap second crossing
columns.means: oncore-host --fake-time and --leap-pending against the image in emulation, across a quarter's end: the image's time and leap seconds through 23:59:60 and after.

statuses.yes: run, and the instrument reached Locked to GPS (or qualified its GPS reference); in a leap second column, it read the leap second as the column says
statuses.partial: run, but not all the way: the note says how far
statuses.in-review: the code to run it is in an open pull request, not yet run
